newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cocoa grind figure higher than expected.
newsitem.headline: German cocoa grind figure higher than expected.

text.p: German cocoa traders said news that grind data for the second quarter of 1997 were only 3.5 percent down from a year earlier showed confectionery manufacturers had been more active than expected.
Confectionery association BDS on Monday put the grind, a key demand indicator, at 57,401.8 tonnes.
"I'm surprised, my forecast was for a five or 10 percent fall," said one trader.
"Chocolate sales are not brilliant and one major processor was not running at full capacity due to the commissioning of new plant in the second quarter.
"I can only assume that other plants had reasonable orders."
Traders said the figure was in line with higher Jan/March 1997 German cocoa import data, published July 4.
Imports, at 84,725 tonnes, were up from 69,593 tonnes a year earlier.
A massive influx in March more than compensated for lower tonnages in January and February, the data showed.
The grind figure would be broadly neutral, especially in the context of western Europe, where a higher-than-expected Dutch grind offset a lower-than-expected British result, traders said.
They also added that western European figures were only part of global cocoa processing trends, which included an increasing shift to grindings at origin.
"We need more comprehensive and more frequent global grindings data," one trader said.
